units.source_text: 八月十五傍晚，明月未升之时，三公主来到佛堂面前，眺望着檐前景色而诵读经文。

en.t: On the evening of the fifteenth day of the eighth month, before the bright moon had risen, the Third Princess came before the Buddha hall, gazed out at the scene beneath the eaves, and recited sutras.

units.source_text: 两三个青年尼僧在佛前献花，供净水杯，汲水，

en.t: Two or three young nuns were offering flowers before the Buddha, setting out cups of pure water, and drawing more water,

units.source_text: 三公主听到这些声音，觉得她们忙着这些背世离俗之事，实甚可哀。

en.t: and when the Third Princess heard these sounds, she felt deeply sorry for them, busy as they were with these acts of renouncing the world and leaving ordinary life behind.

units.source_text: 正在此时，源氏照例来了。

en.t: Just then, Genji came as usual.

units.source_text: 他说：“今夜虫声好繁密啊！”

en.t: He said, "How full and constant the insects sound tonight!"
Then he began softly reciting sutras.

units.source_text: 他念阿弥陀大咒，声音轻微而十分严肃。

en.t: He chanted the great Amida dharani, his voice faint yet very solemn.

units.source_text: 虫声实在繁密，其中铃虫之声宛如摇铃，铿锵可爱。

en.t: The insects truly sang in great profusion, and among them the bell crickets sounded like shaken bells, clear and charming.

units.source_text: 源氏说道：“昔人说秋虫鸣声皆美，而其中松虫最为悦耳。

en.t: Genji said, "People of old said that all autumn insects have beautiful voices, but that the pine cricket is the most pleasing to the ear.

units.source_text: 秋好皇后曾经特地派人到遥远的原野中去搜求松虫，放在院子里。

en.t: Empress Akikonomu once even sent people far out into the fields to search for pine crickets and release them in her garden.

units.source_text: 然而现在能分明听出是松虫的，已经很少了。

en.t: Yet nowadays there are very few whose cry one can clearly recognize as that of a pine cricket.

units.source_text: 可见这虫和它的名字不相称，是一种短命的虫。

en.t: It seems, then, that this insect does not live up to its name, and is a short-lived creature.

units.source_text: 它在深山中或远方原野上的松林中，不惜声音地任情鸣唱，

en.t: Deep in the mountains or in pine groves on distant plains, it sings freely and unstintingly with all its voice,

units.source_text: 无人能够听赏，真乃太疏阔了！

en.t: yet there is no one there to listen and enjoy it; that is truly far too remote and ungracious!

units.source_text: 铃虫则不然，随处皆鸣，这才教人欢喜，真乃亲切可爱的虫。”

en.t: Bell crickets are not like that; they sing everywhere, and that is what makes people glad. They are truly familiar and lovable insects."
Hearing this, the Third Princess softly recited:
